back: A file of lines of characters stored on secondary storage; each line ends with an end-of-line marker.
Data in memory is lost when the program ends; data in a file persists and can be reused or shared.
Open (read, write or append), process (read or write lines), close.
Read: existing data, file must exist. Write: erases old contents. Append: keeps contents and adds to the end.
OPENFILE f FOR READ|WRITE|APPEND; READFILE f, Var; WRITEFILE f, Text; CLOSEFILE f; EOF(f).
WHILE NOT EOF(f) DO: READFILE f, Line … ENDWHILE.
open(name, mode); read(), readline(), write(text); close(); with open(...) as f closes the file automatically.
Lines read are strings: use STR_TO_NUM (int() in Python) before arithmetic and NUM_TO_STR (str()) before writing a number.
Data may be buffered until the file is closed; an open file may be locked for other programs.
